look forward to taking your questions and suggestions. Godrej Properties achieved a booking 
value of INR8,008 crores in the second quarter from the sale of 3,658 units with a total area of 
6.2 million square feet.

total area of 12.3 million square feet. The bookings for the quarter were 6% and 7% lower year-

quarter with sustenance sales growth of 83% year-on-year to INR5,054 crores. Three projects, 
namely Godrej Trilogy in Mumbai, Godrej Vanantara in Bengaluru and Godrej Samaris in 
Gurugram contributed more than INR500 crores each to sustenance sales.  
Godrej Brooklyn Avenue, our project in Hyderabad, launched towards the end of the first 
quarter, also contributed more than INR500 crores to bookings. We only launched 1/3 of our 
expected annual launch pipeline in the first half of the financial year, and we're still able to 
deliver 43% of our annual bookings guidance, highlighting the continued strength of underlying 
demand in the sector.

this month onwards, we remain confident of surpassing our full year guidance across all key 
operating metrics. Projects like Bandra, Sector 63A in Gurugram, Thane Uniabex, our projects 
in Vikhroli, hopefully our project in Ashok Vihar, Noida DMIC, Neopolis, Kharadi 2, 
Mahalunge 2, and Vastrapur as well as new phases of several projects are in the pipeline.

And we therefore, expect the second half of this financial year to be our best ever period for both 
launches and sales. The company's sales were well diversified geographically with key 
contributions from major residential markets. NCR this quarter did just under INR2,000 crores. 
Mumbai did about INR1,900 crores. Bangalore, we did just under INR1,600 crores, about 
INR1,000 crores in Pune, INR700-odd crores in Hyderabad and another INR800 crores in other 
cities during the quarter. It is the seventh consecutive quarter in which Godrej Properties has 
delivered more than INR7,000 crores of booking value and the 13th consecutive quarter in which 
the company has delivered more than INR5,000 crores of booking value. 
 
Godrej Properties also reached its highest ever second quarter and first half collection with 
collections growing by 31% in the quarter to INR5,318 crores and by 25% in the first half to 
INR9,666 crores. Benefiting from the strong collections, operating cash flow in the second 
quarter grew by nearly 300% quarter-on-quarter and by 33% year-on-year to INR1,584 crores. 
 
With that, we get to a half yearly cash flow of INR1,983 crores. Construction and related outflow 
increased by 31% year-on-year in the second quarter and by 42% for the first half of the year. 
We are especially focused on generating strong cash flows and expect INR15,000 crores of cash 
collection and INR7,000 crores of operating cash flow in the second half of the financial year.  
This will allow us to both invest for continued growth while also being free cash flow positive 
for this period. FY28, as we've been indicating, is an important year for the company where the 
exceptional growth of the past 2 years becomes apparent in the reported financials under project 
completion accounting.  
We expect to deliver both positive free cash flow and a 20% reported ROE in financial year '28. 
During the last quarter, we added 1 new project with an estimated saleable area of approximately 
1.1 million square feet and expected booking value of about INR6,000 crores. With this, GPL 
has added four projects with an estimated salable area of about 9 million square feet. 
And an expected booking value of about INR15,500 crores in the first half of the financial year, 
which has gotten us to about 78% of our full year guidance. GPL delivered projects aggregating 
2.5 million square feet in the quarter, and we remain on track for 13.5 million square feet of 
delivery in the full year.  
For the quarter, our total income grew by 38% to INR2,575 crores. EBITDA declined by 72% 
to INR171 crores and net profit declined by 62% to INR154 crores. For the first half, total 
income grew by 13% to INR3,912 crores. EBITDA declined by 53% to INR717 crores and net 
profit declined by 50% to INR504 crores. 
 
This was largely due again to the back-ended nature of deliveries this year, and we expect to see 
positive momentum, particularly in Q4, and then we've already indicated the expectations on the 
P&L for FY '28. We remain extremely excited about the opportunity ahead and we'll seek to 
continue to gain market share through outstanding design, timely delivery and high-quality 
development. On that note, I conclude my remarks. Thank you all for joining us on the call. 
We'd now be happy to take any questions, comments or suggestions you may have.
